name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,375

clue.text: Quibble about abandoning Paris Hilton's broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast reaches us as sound, so we want a word spoken like the one suggested rather than spelt like it

blocks.note: to split is slang for leaving or walking out on someone
Paris Hilton is famous as an heiress to the hotel fortune, one of the heirs

explanation.surface: Someone haggles over the details of Paris Hilton being dropped from a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Paris Hilton's' as 'heirs', said out loud; the possessive becomes the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is the idiom for arguing over trivial distinctions, which is exactly what quibbling means.

clue.text: Get on with Miranda's dad for the most part

indicators.note: taking most but not all of the word means its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: in Shakespeare's The Tempest, Miranda is the daughter of the magician Prospero

explanation.surface: Advice to rub along with Miranda's father as much as you can.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, and getting on in life is the same idea of advancing successfully.

clue.text: Deduce from a refusal to escape from Hell

indicators.note: whatever escapes from the larger word leaves it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: no is the word of refusal
the inferno is a name for hell, as in Dante

explanation.surface: Working out, from being refused, that there is no getting out of Hell.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing NO of INFERNO is the refusal that escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, the standard synonym for deducing.

clue.text: Welsh town embracing plan to have women's refuge

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the town's letters wrap around the others

blocks.note: Hay-on-Wye, the book-festival town on the Welsh border
an idea is a plan or scheme
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A Welsh town is setting up a women's refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay-on-Wye is a small book-festival town on the Welsh border; the plan and the women both go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded place to retreat to, so it serves as a refuge or hiding place.

clue.text: Helpful to first violinist for example

blocks.note: being instrumental in something is being helpful in bringing it about
first abbreviates to 1ST, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is of assistance to the leader of an orchestra's violins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First violinist' looks like one phrase, but the split is after 'first'; the digit in 1ST passes as an I.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays a musical instrument, so a violinist is one example of an instrumentalist.

clue.text: Assumed by Potter about to support Socialist leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
in a down answer, a piece supporting another sits below it, so it comes second

blocks.note: the opening letter of Socialist
to truck is informal for moving along at a leisurely pace, ambling or pottering about

explanation.surface: A political stance adopted by someone named Potter, about to back a socialist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumed' is in the sense of an attitude or pose struck, taken on for show.
explanation.definitionFit: You can strike a pose or attitude, meaning to adopt it, so struck works as the past participle assumed.

clue.text: Tenacity shown by last of joggers after a hard struggle on the way back

indicators.note: travelling on the way back means going the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left
the last of a word is only its final letter

blocks.note: a tug is a hard pull or struggle, as in tug of war
the final letter of joggers

explanation.surface: A jogger at the back shows grit after a tough battle on the return leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes after the reversed struggle, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts is informal for courage and determination, the staying power that tenacity describes.

clue.text: Rib with gibes about Henry's bull

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned around or in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Teasing someone with jibes about Henry's bull, the animal on his farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry's' reads as Henry's animal, but the 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition; bull is nonsense, not a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense or empty talk, and gibberish is meaningless or unintelligible speech.

clue.text: Herschel's discovery of Hyperion for instance initially intrigued astronomers

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: in Greek myth Hyperion was one of the Titans
the first letters of intrigued and astronomers

explanation.surface: Herschel's find of Saturn's moon Hyperion fascinated the astronomers of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyperion is also a moon of Saturn, which makes the astronomy surface plausible; here it is the mythical Titan.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel discovered Titania, the largest moon of Uranus, in 1787.

clue.text: Cliff oddly lacking energy before game

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: go means energy or vigour, as in full of go
the even-placed letters of Cliff, its second and fourth

explanation.surface: Cliff has run out of steam before his match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff oddly lacking energy' looks like one phrase, but energy is a separate piece placed before.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs and balls across a course of holes, so it is a game.

clue.text: Divide amongst several of girl's close-knit group - mostly Native American people

indicators.note: taking only most of the word means its last letter is left off

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, and Di's becomes DIS
a tribe is a close-knit social group
the Ute are a Native American people of the Great Basin

explanation.surface: Sharing something out among a girl's tight circle, mainly Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out or share something among a number of recipients.

clue.text: Box, essentially intact, found in an ancient Greek site

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: to box and to spar are both to fight with fists
the two middle letters of intact

explanation.surface: An unbroken box turns up at an archaeological dig in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container noun, but it is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece in the Peloponnese whose remains are a historic site.

clue.text: Cowardly soldiers interrupting to forswear a previously held belief

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so these letters sit inside the other word

blocks.clueFragment: to forswear a previously held belief
blocks.note: to recant is to withdraw a former opinion publicly
RE is the Royal Engineers, crossword shorthand for soldiers

explanation.surface: Timid troops butt in as someone abandons their old faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers go inside after REC.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic adjective for craven or faint-hearted, often applied to a knight who yielded.

clue.text: With support curtailed, right to publish abroad

indicators.note: to curtail is literally to cut off the tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a prop is a support
a claim is a right or title to something

explanation.surface: Your backing reduced, you have the right to publish overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' is not overseas here: to publish abroad is the old sense of spreading widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, and 'publish abroad' in its older sense means make widely known.

clue.text: Rent bill included in letter

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it

blocks.note: to charter a boat or plane is to rent it
AC abbreviates account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bill for the rent comes enclosed in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill goes inside after CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol such as a letter of the alphabet or a printed sign.

clue.text: Country retreat originally owned by a Scotsman

indicators.note: 'originally' asks for just the opening letter
what is owned is held by its owner, so these letters are held inside the name

blocks.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John, the crossword's typical Scotsman
the first letter of retreat

explanation.surface: A country retreat belongs to a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country retreat' looks like a cottage; country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Liken to keeping death's-head of a friend

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the other letter goes within
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to liken one thing to another is to compare them
the first letter of death

explanation.surface: Comparing a friend to a skull, the death's-head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Death's-head' is a skull, but here it means the head of death.
explanation.definitionFit: Compadre is Spanish-American slang for a companion or buddy, widely used in English.

clue.text: It's played merely to turn 8's heart

indicators.note: turning the word around reads it right to left
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: but can mean only or merely, as in 'but a child'
8 down is TITANIA, and its central letter of seven is the fourth

explanation.surface: A game played simply to reach the heart of answer 8.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 8 is TITANIA, whose middle letter is A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass instrument, so it is something a musician plays.

clue.text: Oblivious Mogul deputy dropping book in river

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so that letter is removed
'in' places the shortened title inside the river

blocks.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
a nawab was a provincial governor under the Mogul emperors in India
B abbreviates book

explanation.surface: A Mughal official loses his book in a river without noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: A nawab was a regional governor serving the Mogul emperors; the river is the Yorkshire Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware means having no knowledge or realisation of something, just as oblivious does.

clue.text: Dicky, 23, extremely earnest about becoming a novice

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the word's letters are disordered
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
'about' means turned round, so the pair is read backwards

blocks.note: 23 across is PHONEY
the first and last letters of earnest

explanation.surface: Someone shaky and fake, though very serious, is turning into a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 23 is PHONEY, rearranged; 'dicky' is British slang for unreliable or shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or new convert, someone just starting out, the same as a novice.

clue.text: River running by state capital

blocks.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A river flows past the seat of state government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a river in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the capital city of the US state of New Jersey.

clue.text: Unidentified witness hugging King Charles at start of trial

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap the arms around, so these letters enclose the royal abbreviation
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to witness is to see
CR is Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher of King Charles
the first letter of trial

explanation.surface: An anonymous witness embraces King Charles as the trial begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unidentified witness' sounds like a court-case phrase, but only 'Unidentified' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept secret is undisclosed and not made known, so its identity remains unidentified.

clue.text: Influential choreographer's opening ignored during her key dance

indicators.note: ignoring the opening means the first letter is left out
something happening during another sits within it

blocks.note: Rudolf Laban, the dance theorist who devised a system of movement notation
taken as written
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A great choreographer's opening sequence is cut from her central dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Laban was a pioneering 20th-century dance theorist; drop his L and put the rest inside HER.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a Cuban dance in slow duple time, famous from Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Counterfeit currency Miles left behind pub

indicators.note: the letter that has left is no longer there, so it is removed

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
currency is money in circulation
M abbreviates miles

explanation.surface: Forged banknotes that Miles abandoned at the back of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' looks like a man's name, but it is the unit, M; 'behind' puts the shortened currency after the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney means fake or not genuine, and counterfeit is forged in imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: Overcome being debarred by party

blocks.note: someone debarred or excluded is out
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Feeling crushed after being barred from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to beat or surpass them, which is what overcoming a rival means.

clue.text: Gain control by blocking doctor's TV show

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in its middle, so it goes inside

blocks.note: to master something is to gain control of it
MD is a Doctor of Medicine
by can mean in, as in 'by night' meaning in the night

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge by obstructing a medic's television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition. Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz with a famous black chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is a long-running British television quiz programme in which contestants answer on a specialist subject.

clue.text: Carry On Teacher at first shown in the centre of Cheltenham

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for the opening letters of the preceding words
the centre of a word is its middle letters
what is shown inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: the two central letters of the ten in Cheltenham
the first letters of On and Teacher

explanation.surface: The film Carry On Teacher is being screened in central Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On Teacher is a 1959 British comedy film; the split falls after 'Carry'. Cheltenham is an English spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, especially a heavy load or a gun, as in toting a bag.

clue.text: Try to pay attention

blocks.note: first meaning: a judge tries, or ..., a case in court
second meaning: to listen to and heed

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to concentrate; the legal sense of trying a case is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hears a case when it tries it, and to hear also means to listen carefully.

clue.text: Against His Excellency accepting Brandt's final argument as relevant

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside
the final letter of the word is the only one kept

blocks.note: to can mean against, as in cheek to cheek or back to the wall
HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
the last letter of Brandt
a point is an argument or proposition made in debate

explanation.surface: An ambassador objects to Willy Brandt's last argument as being pertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against His Excellency' gives two words, and Brandt's letter slips between them. Willy Brandt was the West German chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to the point is pertinent and bears directly on the matter being discussed.
